Behavior change: fetch_blocks_from_peers now returns as soon as no request is in flight, instead of idling until the 4s FETCH_FROM_PEERS_TIMEOUT. This affects two cases: no request was sent because every selected block was already locked, or the last outstanding request failed with no peer left to retry on. Conditions were ideal for the launch, with the atmospheric winds so calm the rocket’s white plume did not dissipate for many minutes. The weather in South Texas is not always comfortable; summers are long and hot. Friday evening was perfect at Starbase. The first stage ascended toward space flawlessly, releasing the upper stage above the Gulf of Mexico. From there, the Starship upper stage ignited its Raptor engines and powered its way into a nominal orbit. This was the second time SpaceX has flown Starship into low-Earth orbit. items.excerpt: NCCL 2.32.3 added TLS 1.3 PSK encryption of its TCP sockets via the process-global ncclSetEncryption . PyTorch has no way to enable it. Adds ProcessGroupNCCL.Options.encryption_psk , honored by nccl2 (which shares the Options class); legacy ProcessGroupNCCL (including shrink) rejects it and torchcomms (including split) raises instead of silently ignoring it. NCCL rereads the key for every new socket, including live communicators', so nccl2 applies it once in the constructor of the first group: later groups (including split children) must pass the same key or none, and a different key or a key on a non-first group raises. Mismatched keys across ranks can hang, as NCCL drops failed handshakes. NCCL validates length (>= 32 bytes); NUL bytes raise ValueError. NCCL < 2.32.3 and ROCm raise. items.excerpt: Video game controllers have come a long way from the days when a vibration motor was enough to make the action in the game feel real. Modern controllers can simulate everything from the recoil of a gun to the resistance of pulling a bowstring — but there's still something missing. They can't reproduce the finer details of touching and handling objects in a virtual world. Researchers from Hunan University and the Chinese Academy of Sciences are looking to change that with ElectroPad , a modified PlayStation 5 controller that makes virtual objects feel more realistic. ElectroPad uses a technique called electrotactile stimulation. By sending carefully controlled electrical pulses through electrodes in contact with the skin, it can create localized sensations that mimic textures, edges, and shapes.
